observations.humor: Buddy’s self-pinned blanket gives him a mistake before his successful kite distraction; the sequence avoids making him merely Neet’s commentator. Neet’s literal duty to follow the kite supplies setup for the snack trick and final relinquishing of sky supervision. Meera waits out an actual firework before amending quiet, with Heather almost spilling chai as a distinct human response. Sensible intervals is a snack callback, not an unrelated closing gag.
observations.voices: Neet’s excitement and literal importance remain distinct from Buddy’s concise practical misdirection. Heather recognizes the crumb through action rather than an explanatory account of dog speech. Meera has an affectionate self-correction. Historical Heather/Meera household is retained; no Sagar insertion.
observations.causality_timing: Neet sees Buddy’s remaining food, Buddy diverts his gaze, eats, swallows, then answers; the image arrives only after the payoff. Heather’s high-flyer answer still directly follows Neet’s aspiration. No dialogue attribution is separated by an illustration. The three pictures punctuate sky, snack and rest rather than crowding individual exchanges.
observations.heart_and_ending: Buddy shares the blanket he carefully arranged; Neet stops tracking lights and accepts rest. The star-only closing picture earns the quiet final sentence, which remains alone after the picture without a new joke. The blanket opening therefore pays off emotionally as well as comically.
observations.complementarity: First picture establishes upward attention and comfort; second redirects attention to a small incriminating crumb; third lowers both dogs fully into sleep. The first two share terrace/chair/blanket geography but depict different gaze targets and narrative outcomes, so the repetition supports continuity.
